newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday that its net international reserves as of October 11 1996, were $15.836 billion, compared with $15.833 billion on October 4.
The central bank said its assets were $3.893 billion as of October 11, compared with $3.758 billion as of October 4.
It said the increase in international assets was due to:
- Revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $159 million
- A net foreign exchange decline of $19 million.
- A net sale of currency to the federal government for $5 million to cover debt servicing charges.
Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose 263 million pesos in the same period.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
